angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 263,670 km at 178.34 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6073 +/- 0.0725 mas (same row, RUWE 1.17): 178.34 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.379 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-317 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract): 263,670 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.403 +/- 0.006 solar masses from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-317 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3387 +/- 5 K from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-317 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-317 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-317.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.886, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
